Design the Sweep to Fit Your Layout

  • Set Pin Target to Parent Row or Parent Section, keeping the whole area still while it sweeps.
  • Set Viewport Height from 0 to 100 percent, fitting the sweep band to your section without clipping.
  • Switch Text Direction to Right to Left for languages like Arabic, keeping the sweep and letter order correct.

Control How Smoothly Your Headline Scrolls

  • Set Scrub Smoothing from 0 to 3 seconds, choosing a tight scroll lock or a soft lag.
  • Adjust Scroll Length up to 5000 pixels, controlling exactly how long the section stays pinned.
  • Leave Respect Reduced Motion on by default, showing a still, centered headline to sensitive visitors.

Turn On Letter Reveal for Impact

  • Set Throw Distance up to 500 percent, sending each letter further before it settles.
  • Control Tilt from 0 to 90 degrees, letting letters rotate in or settle flat.
  • Choose Elastic, Back, Power, Bounce, or None as your settle style, matching the motion to your brand.

Recommended stack

Astro + GSAP

Static-first rendering, custom CSS, isolated animation modules and optional progressive enhancements.

  • Astro components
  • GSAP + ScrollTrigger
  • Custom responsive CSS
  • No React runtime by default
  • Accessible reduced-motion fallback

gsap.to(track, {
  x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - innerWidth),
  ease: "none",
  scrollTrigger: {
    trigger: shell,
    pin: true,
    scrub: 1
  }
});
FAQ

Technical decisions, kept simple.

Why Astro instead of React?+

This site is content-first and animation-heavy, not state-heavy. Astro keeps the output lean while still giving us a component system.

Is GSAP required?+

For the cinematic scroll behavior we are targeting, GSAP + ScrollTrigger gives us predictable timelines, pinning and responsive control.

Will mobile use the same animations?+

Not always. Heavy horizontal/pinned effects can become simpler stacked interactions on small screens for usability and performance.

Can this later move into Laravel?+

Yes. The visual system and motion logic can be ported section by section; the current build avoids framework-specific UI state.
